purpose: Invented, statically determinate T4-U4b cases as request-agnostic case descriptions: every physical input a model 0.6.0 product request needs. Model 0.6.0, its directional SIF input fields and the U4b row kinds are not yet defined, so no product request is frozen here.
claim_fence: Standard claim fence applies (F-PIP-2; claims taxonomy per DEC-081).

number_conventions.binary64_exact: node positions, y_reference components and load components are the binary64 values written here, taken as exact
number_conventions.decimal_targets: outside diameter, wall, mill tolerance, corrosion allowance, E, nu, alpha, bend radius, pressure, k and SIF values are exact decimal targets (the shortest decimal of the written number); their binary64 rounding moves results by about 1e-16 relative, far inside the criterion
number_conventions.bend_angle: each arc's arc.bend_angle_binary64_for_authoring (repeated in the oracle's derived.arc) is the binary64 nearest to the included angle formed from the chord and R, for the bend component that states it

fields.route: exact: a pressure_contract document (identity pressure-2 when defined); preview: a pressure-free document on the preview-physics route (identity preview-physics-2 when defined)
fields.members.kind: straight, or realized_arc (a span bend realized as curved_bend_macro_element)
fields.members.y_reference: on a straight the element-local y reference; on an arc the bow direction (the arc bows toward +y_reference projected normal to the chord)
fields.members.arc: bend_radius R; bend_angle_binary64_for_authoring; bend_component_attachment_node, the arc's authored from node (as in U4a); the bow rule; k
fields.members.directional_sif_user_values: invented i_ip (on M_z, in-plane) and i_op (on M_y, out-of-plane) in the arc's tangent frame
fields.load_case.member_uniform_forces: constant global force per unit length: per unit member length on a straight, per unit arc length on an arc (length_measure)
fields.load_case.pressure_regions: internal pressure p (signed; external zero) over the listed members, each terminal with its closure disposition
fields.supports: one full anchor; the other line end is free

binding_when_0_6_0_is_defined: a builder authors one product request per case from these descriptions (bend components, primitive loads per global component, pressure region and terminals, shear model, SIF fields);

each realized arc becomes one bend component attached at arc.bend_component_attachment_node (the arc's authored from node, as in U4a), referencing the arc's pipe, with bend_radius R, bend angle arc.bend_angle_binary64_for_authoring, the user k and the SIF fields;
the U4b design's row-kind table maps the oracle's agnostic quantity keys to row kinds;
oracle values never move to match a product;
the request SHA-256 values are added to the oracle when the requests exist.

cases.description: planar L line (straight, realized 90 deg left-turn arc R/r_o = 4.56, straight), anchored at A, free tip D; 4.2 MPa with transferring closures; tip force and moment, uniform loads on every member (out-of-plane and in-plane on the arc); distinct section bases

pressure_contract.shear_model_note: every frozen value is identical under euler_bernoulli and timoshenko_annulus_energy_v1: the line is statically determinate, and realized arcs are Euler-Bernoulli under either model

arc.bend_angle_note: the binary64 nearest to the included angle 2 atan2(s, c), s = chord/(2R), c = sqrt(1 - s^2), formed from the binary64 node positions and the decimal R (filled by the generator); the bend component states it
arc.attachment_note: the bend component is attached at the arc's authored from node, as in U4a
arc.bow_rule: the arc bows toward +y_reference projected normal to the chord (the centre lies on the opposite side)
arc.flexibility_factor_note: invented user flexibility factor; no frozen value depends on it because the line is statically determinate (one anchor, free tip)

directional_sif_user_values.note: invented user-supplied directional factors, not code or library data: i_ip multiplies the in-plane moment M_z and i_op the out-of-plane moment M_y of the arc's tangent frame
